clue.text: Centre of important docks, say, in London

definitions.text: Centre of important docks, say, in London

blocks.note: surface reading: the hub of a busy port, a place for ships
setter's reading: docks stands for the similar-sounding docs, short for doctors, so the street where eminent physicians practise

explanation.surface: A guide pointing out the heart of London's great dockland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' tells you docks is to be heard as docs, doctors; the street is famous for private medical consultants.
explanation.definitionFit: This Marylebone street has for centuries housed the consulting rooms of eminent private physicians and specialists.

clue.text: A good score or several scores

blocks.note: first meaning: a century, a fine individual total in cricket
second meaning: a score is twenty, and five of them make this number

explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty, so 'several scores' is a number counted in twenties; in cricket reaching this figure is the batter's landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The number equals five twenties, and a batter making a century has posted an excellent total.

clue.text: About one dock to the North having more space

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading upwards, so the letters run in the opposite order

blocks.note: re is Latin-derived for concerning
the Roman numeral for one
to moor a boat is to tie it up, as at a dock

explanation.surface: A ship berthing at a northern quay finds plenty of room.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of roomy describes a place offering a larger amount of space than another.

clue.text: Provide diversion to harbour

blocks.note: first meaning: amuse an audience or guests
second meaning: hold in mind, as one might a doubt or an idea

explanation.surface: An order to send shipping elsewhere to a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harbour' looks like a noun for a port; here it is the verb meaning to keep a thought or feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: You amuse guests by keeping them happy, and you can also hold or consider an idea in your mind.

clue.text: Prepared for winning at tennis?

definitions.note: describes a player one set ahead

blocks.note: first meaning: arranged or made ready in advance
second meaning, read literally: one set to the good in a tennis match

explanation.walkthrough: A tennis player who has taken more sets than the opponent is ahead by a set, which reads as the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged beforehand has been made ready, and a player leading by one set is literally that.

clue.text: It repeatedly provides stage murmurs

blocks.note: surface reading: something that keeps supplying a sound
setter's reading: actors playing a crowd mutter a garden vegetable's name over and over to mimic background chatter

explanation.surface: Something keeps producing the low muttering heard on a theatre stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Extras in a theatre traditionally say the name of this plant again and again to sound like an indistinct crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage convention has crowd actors repeat this vegetable's name to create meaningless background noise or chatter.

clue.text: I'm a rep round about the big stores

indicators.note: about suggests letters scattered here and there, so they are put into a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A sales representative boasts of doing the rounds of the major department stores.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Latin-style plural of a word for a large retail shop or market centre.

clue.text: The complaint of a man of letters?

definitions.text: The complaint of a man of letters?

blocks.note: surface reading: a grievance or grumble
setter's reading: a complaint is also an ailment, here the one an author's hand suffers from too much penmanship

explanation.surface: A literary figure voices a grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: Complaint means an illness as well as a grumble; a man of letters is an author.
explanation.definitionFit: This painful spasm of the hand muscles comes from prolonged handwriting, the occupational ailment of authors.

clue.text: Dismisses UN tours abroad

indicators.note: abroad can mean widely scattered or astray, so these letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The United Nations sends people packing from its overseas trips.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a fielder who hits the stumps while a batter is short of the crease dismisses them this way.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, breaking the wicket before a batter completes a run ends that batter's innings.

clue.text: Instrument causing politician to be in utter disarray

indicators.note: in places one element inside another
disarray is a state of disorder, so the letters are muddled into a new arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A musical instrument leaves a politician in total chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utter' looks like an adjective meaning total; it is the jumbled word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brass wind instrument with valves and a flared bell, played by buzzing the lips.

clue.text: Had the tenner after a flutter "in an instant"

indicators.note: a flutter is a nervous shaking, so after it the letters are left in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A punter had the ten-pound note straight after placing a small bet.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small bet, which fits the tenner; here it signals rearrangement. A tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means immediately, on the spot, without any delay at all.

clue.text: The tenacious person's reserve

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who hangs on doggedly, like the dog breed bred to dig out prey
second meaning: informal name for a member of Britain's Territorial Army, the volunteer reserve force

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a determined person's reticence; reserve is a soldier in Britain's part-time Territorial Army, nicknamed after a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog breed is famous for stubborn persistence, and Territorial Army volunteers carry the same nickname.

clue.text: No trees here it's plain

blocks.note: surface reading: an observation that a spot has no woodland
setter's reading: plain is a noun, a broad flat grassland such as the North American kind

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that obviously no trees grow in this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plain' reads as obvious, but it is the noun for flat open country.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a vast area of flat, treeless grassland, especially in central North America.

clue.text: One well up in what's legally added

blocks.note: first meaning: a person sitting high on a horse
second meaning: an extra clause appended to a document or bill

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly versed in legal additions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well up in' looks like knowledgeable about; it splits into a mounted person and a legal appendix.
explanation.definitionFit: A horseman sits up in the saddle, and an appended clause to a contract or bill bears the same name.

clue.text: Outline a stupid tax

blocks.note: taken as written
dumb means slow-witted
rates are a local property tax

explanation.surface: Someone sketches out a foolish levy.
explanation.definitionFit: To sketch or foreshadow something faintly, giving only a vague indication of its form.

clue.text: Hives not restricted to apiarists

blocks.note: surface reading: homes for bees, the business of beekeepers
setter's reading: hives is also an itchy skin rash, which anyone can get

explanation.surface: Beehives can be owned by people other than beekeepers.
explanation.walkthrough: Apiarists are beekeepers; hives here is the medical name for nettle rash.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical term for an itchy raised skin rash, also called nettle rash.

clue.text: King holding a second cut due for a roasting?

definitions.note: describes the answer rather than naming it

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so one part goes around the rest

blocks.note: Cnut, or Canute, was an English king
taken as written
abbreviation for second
to hew is to chop or cut

explanation.surface: A monarch, having had a second trim, is in line for harsh criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: A roasting is a scolding in the surface, but these kernels are often roasted.
explanation.definitionFit: This kidney-shaped kernel is usually sold roasted, so it is ready for the oven treatment.

clue.text: PC rules in order to obtain regard for morality

indicators.note: putting things in order means arranging them properly, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A police constable keeps to the rules so that he is seen as ethical.
explanation.definitionFit: A moral hesitation or qualm arising from conscience about whether an action is right.

clue.text: An arch that can be raised, surprisingly

definitions.text: An arch that can be raised, surprisingly

blocks.clueFragment: An arch that can be raised
blocks.note: surface reading: a curved structure in building, perhaps a lifting bridge
setter's reading: the curve of hair above the eye goes up when someone is astonished

explanation.surface: Remarkably, an arch can be lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' seems to comment on the engineering, but it describes when this arch goes up.
explanation.definitionFit: The arched line of hair above each eye lifts when a person shows astonishment or disbelief.

clue.text: Part of premises a London beautician occupies

definitions.note: a phrase for what a beautician occupies, standing for a noun

indicators.note: part of tells you to take only a run of letters from inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, the second word and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A beauty parlour takes up part of a building in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairdressers and beauticians work in an establishment of this name, their place of business.

clue.text: Artificial flower ring for the hair?

definitions.note: describes what the answer is used on

blocks.note: sham means fake
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Po is in Italy
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A fake bloom woven into a circlet worn as a hair ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' is a crossword favourite for a river, something that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid soap used for washing the hair is the product being suggested here.

clue.text: Leaves football body in league with penultimate loss

indicators.note: losing the penultimate means dropping the letter just before the last
in puts one element inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
the Football Association governs English football

explanation.surface: The football authority quits, allied with a league that has just suffered a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb about quitting; it is the noun, and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage, the collective mass of a plant's leaves, is what this word denotes.

clue.text: Stuffy, bald cockney

indicators.note: Londoners of the East End traditionally drop the h at the start of words

blocks.note: having no hair on the head

explanation.surface: A cockney who is stuffy and has no hair.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney is a working-class East Londoner whose accent drops the h.
explanation.definitionFit: A room without fresh ventilation feels close and stale, lacking circulating air.

clue.text: Ropy material in recut sails

indicators.note: cutting something again reshapes it, so these letters are put into a new pattern

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Poor-quality fabric found in sails that have been tailored afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ropy' is British slang for shoddy, but here it means used for making rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Fibre from an agave plant used to make rope and twine, hence a cord-making material.

clue.text: Noisy one making bid (one-off)

indicators.note: off means removed, so the named letter is taken away

blocks.note: someone who puts in a claim
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A loud bidder at an auction makes a single, unrepeated offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One-off' looks like a single occasion; it splits into the numeral and an instruction to remove it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare word for loud and insistent, clamouring for attention.

clue.text: Written on once

blocks.note: surface reading: something penned a single time
setter's reading: the material that ancient scribes wrote upon in former times

explanation.surface: Something was written just one time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' reads as a single time, but it means formerly; this reed-based sheet was the writing surface of ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancient Egyptians made sheets from this reed to write upon, long before modern paper.

clue.text: Substitute traveller's material

blocks.note: a travelling salesman is a sales representative
lace is a fabric

explanation.surface: A replacement for a travelling salesman's cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something new in the position of another thing, swapping it out.

clue.text: Don't tamper with spring

blocks.note: surface reading: advice not to interfere
setter's reading: a spring is a source of water, so leave the water source alone

explanation.surface: A warning not to fiddle with a coiled spring.
explanation.walkthrough: A spring is a water source; the idiom means leave things as they are, and literally says leave the water source untouched.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom advises leaving a satisfactory situation unchanged rather than risk making it worse by meddling.
